key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Days to weeks, often follows viral illness. LOCATION: Chest (retrosternal or left-sided). DURATION: Continuous over days. CHARACTER: Dull ache, pressure, or sharp pleuritic pain. AGGRAVATING: Exertion. RELIEVING: Rest. TIMING: Progressive over days. SEVERITY: Variable, 4-7/10. KEY POSITIVES: Recent viral illness (URI, GI illness) 1-3 weeks prior, dyspnea, fatigue, palpitations, fever, young patient. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT typical exertional angina pattern, NOT elderly (usually younger patients).

red_flags: Severe dyspnea or heart failure symptoms
Young patient with myocardial infarction (MI)-like presentation
Family history of sudden cardiac death
